newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger in very thin market.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger in very thin market.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, outperforming their U.S. counterparts, but dealers said Canadian gains were exaggerated by a thin market.

"It's just a very illiquid market as we go into next Tuesday," said Will Sutherland, vice-president of fixed-income with Altamira Investment Services. "There has obviously been a buyer in the long end but it was selective and everyone is trying to chase down where it's coming from."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.25 at C$101.65 to yield 7.850 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which fell 13/32 to yield 7.05 percent.
The spread between the benchmarket bonds narrowed to 80 basis points from 85 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
"Everything is whipped around. Volumes are thin. The market's running scared and there's no liquidity," said one Toronto trader. "It's all curve games."
Investors are looking ahead to the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve on Tuesday and sentiment is divided as to whether the Fed will tighten.
Uncertainty about the possibility of a Fed hike is keeping many investors on the sidelines, analysts said.
In Canada, investors are also looking ahead to the release tomorrow morning of retail sales data for July, analysts said.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.20 to C$97.34 to yield 7.374 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 7/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds narrowed 52 basis points from 57 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.88 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.24 percent.
